lead.headline: Isaias, season's first hurricane, bears down on the Gulf Coast
lead.dek: Hurricane warning runs from Ocean Springs, Miss., to Florida's Bay-Gulf county line; two states declare emergencies
body: Isaias strengthened into the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season late Wednesday and is forecast to come ashore between the Mississippi coast and the Florida Panhandle late Friday or early Saturday, the National Hurricane Center said, with a hurricane warning posted from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to Florida's Bay-Gulf county line.

At 5 a.m. ET Thursday the center put Isaias about 420 miles south-southwest of the mouth of the Mississippi River with top sustained winds of 80 mph, moving east-northeast at 9 mph and still strengthening. It forecast a peak surge of 5 to 7 feet from Ocean Springs to Indian Pass, Florida, and in Mobile Bay, and 3 to 7 inches of rain, locally 10, along the coast.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency for 25 counties and Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey for 40; Gulf Shores and Orange Beach, Alabama, urged voluntary evacuations, NBC News reported. Isaias formed more than four months into the season, nearly tying the 1905 record for the latest first Atlantic hurricane, a lull meteorologists tie to a strong El Nino, CBS News said.

briefs.headline: Texas executes Jamaal Howard after Pike-based appeal fails
briefs.summary: Howard, 46, was pronounced dead at 8:03 p.m. Wednesday in Huntsville for the 2000 killing of clerk Vickie Swartout; the Supreme Court denied a late appeal citing Tennessee's failed execution and Texas's pentobarbital.

briefs.headline: FBI arrests Minnesota man, 18, over alleged Mall of America plot
briefs.summary: A complaint filed Wednesday says Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud was arrested Tuesday in Richfield buying an AK-47 and 200 rounds from an undercover agent; prosecutors say he eyed an Oct. 24 festival at the mall.

briefs.headline: FDA says mifepristone safety review will not finish until March
briefs.summary: In a Wednesday filing in Louisiana's lawsuit over mail-order abortion pills, the Justice Department said study results are due mid-December and no new restrictions will come before the March report.

briefs.headline: Fed minutes show most officials expect another hike by year-end
briefs.summary: Minutes of the Sept. 15-16 meeting, released Wednesday, show a 12-0 vote to lift the target range to 3.75%-4% and most participants judging another increase 'would likely be appropriate by year end.'

briefs.headline: Saudis say Houthi airport attacks kill 3; new Riyadh claim
briefs.summary: Saudi officials said one person died at Riyadh's airport Wednesday and two at Abha, with 36 wounded; the Houthis claimed a new Riyadh missile strike Thursday, unconfirmed by Riyadh.

briefs.headline: Pryluky toll rises to 22 as rescuers clear rubble
briefs.summary: Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Thursday that 22 people, five of them children, died in Wednesday's missile strike on the five-story block and 54 were hurt, AP reported.

briefs.headline: U.S. prepares torture charges against Maduro and wife
briefs.summary: A U.S. official said prosecutors expect to charge the ousted Venezuelan leader and Cilia Flores over the alleged torture of detained Americans, possibly Thursday, DW reported.

briefs.headline: U.S. opens direct talks with Myanmar junta, officials say
briefs.summary: Reuters reported, citing seven current and former officials, that a State Department official met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyitaw Sept. 15-16, with talks focused on scam centers.

briefs.headline: Trump approves FEMA aid for three counties' August floods
briefs.summary: Individual assistance covers Fayette, Harrison and Kanawha counties for the Aug. 14-18 floods; 11 counties get public assistance for July 21 storms, and a Boone-Logan appeal was denied again.

briefs.headline: House committee gives Flock until Friday to answer questions
briefs.summary: Government Organization members wrote Monday that the company's Sept. 1 reply skipped many of their 19 questions from August, and said subpoenas or compelled testimony could follow.

briefs.headline: Morrisey enters state in bid to host federal Space Academy
briefs.summary: The governor announced the bid Wednesday at the I-79 Technology Park in Fairmont; applications are due Oct. 26, and the state is taking site ideas at wvspaceacademy.com.

briefs.headline: Pack urges special session to suspend West Virginia gas tax
briefs.summary: Treasurer Larry Pack told WSAZ Wednesday that lawmakers could act in 24 to 48 hours after Ohio suspended its 38.5-cent tax through January; Morrisey's office said it is reviewing options.

regional.item: Cabell's school board approved about $418,000 Tuesday to replace Huntington High's water-damaged gym floor.
Vandalia Health and Mary Free Bed broke ground Wednesday on a $50 million rehab hospital across from CAMC General.
Constellium Ravenswood's Artemis II aluminum plates won the inaugural Coolest Thing Made in WV award Wednesday.
Summers County ARH got a walk-through weapons scanner Tuesday, a day after Beckley ARH was first in the system.

away.item: A seven-person archaeology team began digging around the Bennington Battle Monument Tuesday, ahead of a multi-year restoration.

hotspots.item: Secretary of State Kris Warner stopped at the Webster County Clerk's office Sept. 23 to check Nov. 3 election preparations, the Echo reported Tuesday.
Topsail Beach reopened the Topsail Nature Preserve, its beach and parking Wednesday after a contractor finished herbicide treatment of invasive common reed.

briefs.headline: Bomb threat empties DP Todd Secondary in Prince George
briefs.summary: A threat received about 1 p.m. Wednesday sent students and staff next door to Heritage Elementary, where they were dismissed at 2 p.m.; Prince George RCMP said the investigation was in its early stages.

briefs.headline: Prince George advance polls open again today, 8 to 8
briefs.summary: Day two of advance voting runs 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. at the Civic and Conference Centre; chief election officer Ethan Anderson said voters need two pieces of ID, not photo ID. Two more days follow Oct. 14-15.

briefs.headline: Eby pitches $1M tariff loans as Doerkson promises PST cut
briefs.summary: In Surrey Wednesday, NDP Leader David Eby promised interest-free loans of up to $1 million for tariff-hit businesses; Conservative Leader Lorne Doerkson pledged to drop the PST on machinery and approve capital projects in 120 days.

briefs.headline: B.C. starts fall vaccines as flu season arrives early
briefs.summary: The province launched its fall immunization campaign Wednesday with an enhanced flu shot and an RSV vaccine for seniors; the BCCDC said an early rise in cases is driven by H1N1. Higher-risk appointments begin Oct. 13.

briefs.headline: Ottawa shelves MAID for mental illness alone indefinitely
briefs.summary: Justice Minister Sean Fraser said Wednesday fall legislation will extend the exclusion, due to lapse in March 2027, and allow advance requests for people who will lose capacity. Dying With Dignity called it 'profoundly disappointing.'

briefs.headline: Moe and Smith reject Musk's call for Prairie separation
briefs.summary: After Elon Musk posted Wednesday that Alberta and Saskatchewan 'should separate too,' Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe replied 'No' and Alberta's Danielle Smith said she strongly disagrees; Alberta's referendum is Oct. 19.

briefs.headline: Crew-12 undocks from station for Thursday splashdown
briefs.summary: Meir, Hathaway, Adenot and Fedyaev left the station's Harmony module aboard Dragon at 8:05 a.m. EDT Wednesday; NASA targets splashdown off California about 11:34 a.m. ET today.

briefs.headline: Gut microbe molecule cuts artery plaque in mice
briefs.summary: A compound made by Bacteroides uniformis halved arterial plaque in mice by blocking the same liver enzyme statins target, a Sun Yat-sen University team reported in Nature on Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Solar Orbiter traces a magnetic switchback to the Sun
briefs.summary: ESA said Thursday the spacecraft flew through a large S-shaped kink in the solar wind and found charged oxygen and carbon that could only have formed in hot loops at the Sun's surface, in Nature Astronomy.

briefs.headline: Rare brain-abscess fungus cases rose fourfold in two years
briefs.summary: Detections of Cladophialophora bantiana at a University of Washington lab rose from one to five a year through 2023 to 14 in 2025, UW and CDC researchers reported in MMWR; the mold kills 60% to 70% of patients.

briefs.headline: Watchdog rates ChatGPT for Teens an 'unacceptable risk'
briefs.summary: Common Sense Media said Wednesday the teen version failed three of its five crisis 'red lines' and kept nudging users to keep chatting; OpenAI said the testing may have run before parental controls activated.

briefs.headline: CrowdStrike ties Korean bank breaches to AI hacking tool
briefs.summary: A likely Chinese-speaking attacker used ARTEX, an open-source AI penetration-testing tool, to take data from South Korean financial firms from late September, CrowdStrike said Wednesday; The Decoder said Shinhan Bank lost 25,000 records.

briefs.headline: Man gets 18 months for AI-song streaming fraud
briefs.summary: Michael Smith, 54, of North Carolina, was sentenced Tuesday for using thousands of bot accounts to stream hundreds of thousands of AI-generated songs, the Justice Department said; he must repay over $8 million.

weather_ear: Jim Claudtore has Thursday's forecast at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster carries no regional line today; Crew-12 is due to splash down off California about 11:34 a.m.
